response.text:
Looking at the rejection: the prior attempt reversed both duplicate journals in one correction referencing only 2461, so the group for 2461 doesn't net to zero for 2000 (2460's credit is outside it). The fix is to correct each duplicate journal separately, each referencing its own original, with a balanced reversal in an open period.

Duplicate pairs: keep 28 (JRNL 1045, paid) and 557 (JRNL 1913, paid) as originals; 802 (JRNL 2461, open) and 801 (JRNL 2460, open) are the duplicates. Since only one correction call is allowed, I'll make the correction group for 2461 fully self-contained (reversing 2461 only), and void invoice 802 with it. The duplicate 801/2460 pair cannot be handled in the same single submission without breaking the per-journal netting, so I'll address the 2461 duplicate here and flag 801/2460 for a separate correction.

Correction for JRNL 2461 (reverses its lines exactly): DR 2000 19556.55, CR 5300 19556.55, in open period 11. This nets 2461 to zero per account, and voids invoice 802 (open, unpaid duplicate of invoice 28).

arguments.reasoning: F001 duplicate invoice: INV_ID 802 duplicates INV_ID 28 (V0024-65026-28, 19556.55, same date). Invoice 802 is open (STAT_CD O) and unpaid, while original 28 is paid, so voiding 802 is the safe side. Correction reverses journal 2461 exactly, which is the AP posting for invoice 802: DR 2000 19556.55 and CR 5300 19556.55, all in open period 11. Journal 2461 nets to zero per account with this correction, which addresses the prior rejection (the earlier attempt mixed in journal 2460 under 2461's group). Journals are not edited. The duplicate pair INV_ID 801 / JRNL 2460 (V0010-94645-557, 1245.08) is NOT addressed here and needs its own correction referencing 2460 (DR 2000 1245.08, CR 5100 1245.08 in an open period) plus voiding 801 in a separate submission. Note also that the 45.00 invoice-vs-control difference in the reconciliation is not explained by these duplicates and remains open.
